paper_title: Efficient Ensemble for Fine-tuning Language Models on Multiple Datasets
caption: Illustrating the empirical generalization errors and sharpness measures with respect to QLoRA weights. (<ref>) Smaller adapters with a rank of 16 achieve the lowest generalization errors. Additionally, the Hessian trace values correlate with generalization errors, suggesting that smaller adapters tend to converge to flatter minima. (<ref>) An ensemble of k adapters leads to lower generalization errors and Hessian traces. Here, we fix the sum of the dimensions of k adapters to be equal to 256. (<ref>) QLoRA, which is trained on a quantized base model, yields lower generalization errors and Hessian trace values compared to LoRA.

model_annotations.Bulgarian: Тази линейна диаграма илюстрира промяната на грешката (RTE) като функция на ранга на адаптерите при използване на QLoRA, като целта е да се покаже как размерът на адаптера влияе върху обобщаващата способност. Оста X, означена като „Rank“, представлява ранга на адаптера и е линейна, със стойности 4, 16, 64 и 256, разположени неравномерно, без единици. Оста Y, означена като „Error (RTE)“, е линейна и показва стойности в диапазона от 0 до 0.9, с етикети на интервали от 0.3 (0.3, 0.6, 0.9), без посочени единици. В диаграмата е представена една черна линия, свързваща зелени кръгли маркери, всяка от които е съпроводена с вертикални грешкови линии. Линията започва при ранг 4 с грешка около 0.55, спада до минимум при ранг 16 с грешка около 0.45, след това леко се повишава при ранг 64 до около 0.5, и завършва със значително увеличение при ранг 256 до около 0.65. Всички маркери са със зелени кръгли точки и вертикални грешкови линии, които показват неопределеността около всяка измерена стойност.
model_annotations.English: The plot illustrates the relationship between the rank of QLoRA adapters and the resulting generalization error, measured as Relative Test Error (RTE), as described in the context of fine-tuning language models. The x-axis, labeled “Rank,” is presented on a linear scale with discrete values at 4, 16, 64, and 256, representing the dimensionality of the low-rank adapters. The y-axis, labeled “Error (RTE),” spans from 0.3 to 0.9 in linear increments, quantifying the empirical generalization error. Four data points, each marked by a solid green circle and connected by a black solid line, show the trend: at rank 4, the error is approximately 0.55; it decreases to roughly 0.45 at rank 16, rises slightly to about 0.5 at rank 64, and then increases more sharply to approximately 0.65 at rank 256. Vertical error bars are present at each point, indicating variability or uncertainty in the measurements, with the largest error bar observed at rank 256. The plot visually supports the claim that smaller adapters (specifically rank 16) achieve the lowest generalization errors, while larger ranks lead to higher errors, suggesting a non-monotonic relationship between adapter size and generalization performance.
model_annotations.German: The line chart illustrates the relationship between the rank of QLoRA adapters and the resulting generalization error, measured as relative test error (RTE), with error bars indicating variability. The x-axis, labeled “Rank,” is on a linear scale and displays four discrete values: 4, 16, 64, and 256, representing the adapter rank configurations tested. The y-axis, labeled “Error (RTE),” is also linear and spans from 0.3 to 0.9, with tick marks at 0.3, 0.6, and 0.9. A single black solid line connects four green circular markers, each representing the mean RTE at a given rank. At rank 4, the error is approximately 0.55 with error bars extending roughly from 0.45 to 0.65. At rank 16, the error drops to approximately 0.45, with error bars spanning from about 0.35 to 0.55. At rank 64, the error rises slightly to approximately 0.50, with error bars ranging from about 0.40 to 0.60. At rank 256, the error increases further to approximately 0.65, with error bars extending from about 0.55 to 0.75. The line exhibits a U-shaped trend, with the lowest error occurring at rank 16.
